title: The Riverside Plot

headings.text: Record harvest at the autumn show
Plot 14: a first year without digging
Plot 52: saving your own tomato seed

key_sentences: This year's autumn show drew 214 entries from 61 plot holders, the largest number since the society was founded in 1974.
She praised the quality of the root vegetables and singled out the onions as the best she had seen this season.
Eleven young growers showed decorated marrows, sunflower heads and miniature gardens laid out in seed trays.
The committee thanks all members who kept to the watering rota, which meant that no plot was left without water for more than two days.
At the general meeting members agreed to keep the annual rent at £38 for a full plot and £21 for a half plot.
Rents are due by 1 February and can be paid at the trading hut on Sunday mornings.
Instead of digging, they covered the ground with cardboard and a thick layer of compost.
Harry Blunt has grown the same plum tomato for twenty-two years from his own seed.
Members can collect a free packet of his seed at the November swap.
Leave them in the box at the trading hut or send them to the newsletter editor.

list_items.text: 1 November: bulb and seed swap at the trading hut, 10:00
15 November: working party on the boundary hedges
6 December: mince pies and plot photographs in the pavilion
7 February: general meeting at St Anne's church hall
• The trading hut now sells peat-free compost at £6.50 a bag.
• Please keep the main track clear for the delivery lorry on Thursday mornings.
– Cars may park in the lay-by beside the gate instead.
• Lost: a green-handled pruning saw near plot 30, please return it to the hut.
